framing.lineOfInquiry: Rajesh Singh (P00269) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE031
framing.alternate: Rajesh Singh (P00269) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Rajesh Singh was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 7 other days (22 Apr – 03 Jun), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Rajesh Singh was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak
alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Rajesh Singh's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: In contact with Karan Dhillon since 2025-04-10, 27 days before the incident (3 calls, 5 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Komal Gill since 2025-04-11, 26 days before the incident (1 calls, 3 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Manpreet Bajwa since 2025-04-16, 21 days before the incident (4 calls, 6 messages) — a long-standing relationship
Contact around the incident (12) is close to the normal baseline (≈15.0), with no unusual spike

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset
The money has a legitimate explanation

comparison.verdict: Open: the line of inquiry (0.00) and the strongest alternate — A2 was near the scene for a routine reason (0.27) — are similarly supported. The tests below would separate them.
settleWith: A2 — Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).
A6 — Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.
